# E0611: C library that isn't found

The system's loader finds each library of `link` as `libNAME.dylib` on macOS and `libNAME.so` on Linux. Install the library, or check its name: `link = ["z"]` names zlib.

- Rule: [`c.finding-libraries`](../../reference/20-builds.md#c.finding-libraries)
- Reported at: the library's string in `link`.
- Tier: `systems`, checked in the `items` phase

## What the compiler prints

The program [`E0611_c_library_that_isn_t_found`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0611_c_library_that_isn_t_found):

`src/main.lt`:

```stilt fragment
use std.c

extern fn crc32(crc: u64, buf: c.Ptr<u8>, len: u32) -> u64

pub fn checksum(data: List<u8>) -> u64 {
  let len = data.len().wrap_to_u32()
  unsafe because "crc32 reads len bytes from buf, which with_ptr keeps alive for the call" {
    data.with_ptr(|p| crc32(0, p, len))
  }
}
```

`stilt.toml`:

```text
[package]
name = "zip"
link = ["zlib"]
```

What `stilt check` prints for it:

```text
── C LIBRARY THAT ISN'T FOUND ────────────────────────── stilt.toml:3:9  [E0611]

The C library `zlib` isn't found: the system's loader finds no libzlib:

  3 │ link = ["zlib"]
    │         ^^^^^^

The system's loader finds each library of `link` as `libNAME.dylib` on macOS and
`libNAME.so` on Linux. Install the library, or check its name: `link = ["z"]`
names zlib.
```
